background.text: I want to switch gears a little bit. You've been very vocal about the Washington NFL team and the changing of the name. And of course, it's a significant victory that they've said that they will do that, a victory for activists and critics. I'm curious, though, in this moment of reckoning, there's been a lot of changes like that that are significant, but they're on the surface, changing a name and not necessarily dealing with the systemic issues in our society. ground_truth: Well, I think that it's progress, right? We have, I mean, for decades, not just, it didn't just happen in the last few years, but for decades, Indian activists have been working to bring attention to this issue. And, you know, you have really stubborn people like the owner of the Washington NFL team, who essentially was in denial about what the name of his football team was doing. I think that Native American activists have been present as long as, you know, the Europeans have been working to colonize us. We're just sort of in a new phase, I guess. What I think it does is it brings attention to the need for all of us as Americans to think about this history. Native American history is American history. And since George Floyd died, God rest his soul, we've been dealing with the reckoning in our country about, you know, what do we stand for? Are we really, you know, do we really want liberty and justice for all? Do we really want these things? Do we really want America to be a place where everybody can be successful? And we're getting the answer back that no, only certain people deserve to be successful. And so it's important for people to rise up and demand change. And I think that's incredibly good. And the naming of this football team, even though we had been fighting for it for a long, long time, it was timely to push it even more. And finally, you know, it shouldn't take a huge social movement and corporate sponsors to, you know, threaten to threaten, you know, their, to threaten the team for them to change the name. But, but clearly, that's what it took for this. And I think that it's a good time for all of us to reflect on, on the true history of our country.
